newsitem.title: UK: Copper forecast at 75 cent/lb in 1998 - Billiton.
newsitem.headline: Copper forecast at 75 cent/lb in 1998 - Billiton.

text.p: Copper prices are forecast to fall substantially over the next two years, with cash values expected to average 75 cents per pound ($1,653 a tonne) in 1998, according to Billiton Metals in their base metals review.
The outlook for other base metals was mixed, with bullish potential seen for zinc and aluminium, flat prospects for nickel and tin and a bearish outlook for lead.
"We believe that the (copper) market will record a pretty hefty surplus over the next two years," the report said.
Billiton forecast a Western world supply surplus of 75,000 tonnes in 1996, 400,000 tonnes in 1997 and 450,000 in 1998.
Cash copper was forecast to fall to 90 cents/lb in 1997 from 103 cents in in 1996, and again to 75 cents in 1998.
Billiton was also bearish for lead, with prices expected to drop to 34 cents/lb next year from 35.5 cents in 1996 and again to 29 cents in 1998.
Nickel was forecast to drop to $3.30 per pound in 1997 from $3.43 this year before recovering slightly to $3.50 in 1998.
The outlook for tin was also fairly flat, with cash values expected to average $2.90 per pound in 1997 and $2.75 in 1998, little changed from $2.80 in 1996.
Billiton was more bullish for aluminium and zinc.
Aluminium was forecast to rise to 70 cents in 1997 and 75 cents in 1998 from 68 cents in 1996.

Although stocks are not expected to fall to levels "consistent with a sustained rise in prices", Billiton said "there is scope for a pick up from the present torpor when consumers...return to the market in force."
Zinc was pegged to increase to 53 cents next year and 58 cents a lb the year after from 46.6 cents in 1996.
Stronger demand next year will reduce stocks to "more manageable levels" by the end of 1997, Billiton said.
